evidence: Rick Derringer is credited as producer on Yankovic's albums from his self-titled 1983 debut through 'Off the Deep End' (1992), after which Yankovic took over production himself; Derringer has discussed re-playing the guitar solo on 'Eat It' (1984) himself rather than sampling it.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Derringer's own hit is straightforward hard rock guitar. On 'Eat It' he applies the same playing to a note-for-note re-creation of someone else's solo, the session-guitarist skill his solo career doesn't usually call for.

explanation.age7: Rick Derringer, a rock guitar player, produced Weird Al's albums for about ten years and even replayed a famous guitar solo for one of his songs.
explanation.age13: Derringer produced every Weird Al Yankovic album from 1983 to 1992, and personally re-played Michael Jackson's 'Beat It' guitar solo for the 'Eat It' parody rather than using a sample.
explanation.adult: A straightforward producer-to-artist credit spanning nearly a decade, notable mainly for how much of a stylistic detour it was from Derringer's own hard rock catalogue, filed here as crossLineage since Yankovic sits outside the enum's genre lineages entirely.
